lem-ip-compact-support-fourier-laplace-i:
## Statement

Let $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$ and, for $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$, define $F(z)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}f(x)e^{-2\pi i(x_1z_1+x_2z_2)}\,dx$ using the compact-support Riemann integral on any rectangle containing $\operatorname{supp}f$. This value is independent of the containing rectangle. Each coordinate slice of $F$ is entire, with $\frac{\partial F}{\partial z_j}(z)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}(-2\pi ix_j)f(x)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot z}\,dx$ for $j=1,2$, and the restriction of $F$ to $\mathbb R^2$ is the compact-support Fourier transform in the stated line-normal convention. The proof uses no Countable Choice.
def-ip-visible-covector-for-limited-angl:
## Definition

Let $\Theta\subset S^1$ be a nonempty proper open set of line normals, assume $\theta\in\Theta$ if and only if $-\theta\in\Theta$, and assume $S^1\setminus\overline{\Theta}$ contains a nonempty open arc. The measured line with normal $\theta$ and signed offset $s$ is $\ell_{\theta,s}=\{y\in\mathbb R^2:y\cdot\theta=s\}$. Identify the nonzero cotangent vectors of the Euclidean plane with pairs $(x,\xi)\in\mathbb R^2\times(\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\})$. Such a covector is visible from $\Theta$ when $\xi/|\xi|\in\Theta$, and invisible when $\xi/|\xi|\notin\Theta$. The associated measured Fourier wedge is

$$W_\Theta=\{\sigma\theta:\theta\in\Theta,\ \sigma\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\}.$$
def-ip-schwartz-radon-transform:
## Definition

For $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$, $\theta=(\theta_1,\theta_2)\in S^1$, $s\in\mathbb R$, and $\theta^\perp=(-\theta_2,\theta_1)$, define $R_{\mathcal S}f(\theta,s)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(s\theta+t\theta^\perp)\,dt$, where the absolutely convergent integral is with respect to one-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Here $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$ is the space of smooth complex functions for which every seminorm $\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^2}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|$, for multi-indices $\alpha,\beta$, is finite. The parameter $\theta$ is the unit normal to the line, so $(\theta,s)$ and $(-\theta,-s)$ represent the same unoriented line. Under the Axiom of Countable Choice, the Lebesgue integral in this definition agrees on compactly supported smooth inputs with the compact-support Riemann line integral, so the normalization is the same.
lem-ip-schwartz-radon-well-defined:
## Statement

For every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$ and every $\theta\in S^1$, the defining line integral for $R_{\mathcal S}f(\theta,s)$ converges absolutely for every $s\in\mathbb R$, and $s\mapsto R_{\mathcal S}f(\theta,s)$ belongs to $\mathcal S(\mathbb R)$. For each pair of nonnegative integers $k,N$, its $k$th derivative is bounded by $C_{k,N}(1+|s|)^{-N}$ with a finite constant $C_{k,N}$ independent of $s$ and $\theta$.
lem-ip-limited-angle-radon-data-is-l2-on:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a nonempty bounded open set, let $\Theta\subset S^1$ be measurable, and use arc-length measure $d\theta$ on $S^1$. For every $f\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb C)$, the function $(\theta,s)\mapsto R_{\mathcal S}f(\theta,s)$ belongs to $L^2(\Theta\times\mathbb R,d\theta\,ds)$ and satisfies $\|R_{\mathcal S}f\|_{L^2(\Theta\times\mathbb R)}^2\le \operatorname{diam}(\Omega)\,|\Theta|\,\|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^2)}^2$.
cor-ip-limited-angle-compact-support-uni:
## Statement

Let $\Theta\subset S^1$ be a nonempty open set of unit line normals and let $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)$. If the line integral $Rf(\theta,s)$ is zero for every $\theta\in\Theta$ and $s\in\mathbb R$, then $f$ is zero everywhere. The assertion holds without Countable Choice.
prop-ip-limited-angle-data-no-holder-sta:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded open set containing a closed ball $K=\overline B_R(x_0)$ of positive radius, and let $\Theta\subset S^1$ be a nonempty open antipodally symmetric set. Write $\theta^\perp=(-\theta_2,\theta_1)$ and, for a Schwartz function $g$, define $R_{\mathcal S}g(\theta,s)=\int_{\mathbb R}g(s\theta+t\theta^\perp)\,dt$; use the same integral for smooth functions supported in $K$. Suppose a unit vector $v\in S^1$ satisfies $c:=\inf_{\theta\in\Theta}|v\cdot\theta^\perp|>0$. For each smooth complex function $u$ supported in $K$, define $\|u\|_{H^1}:=(\|u\|_2^2+\|\partial_1u\|_2^2+\|\partial_2u\|_2^2)^{1/2}$ using Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^2$, and set $\|R_\Theta u\|_D:=(\int_\Theta\int_{\mathbb R}|R_{\mathcal S}u(\theta,s)|^2\,ds\,d\theta)^{1/2}$, where $ds$ is Lebesgue measure and $d\theta$ is arc-length measure. For every $M>0$ there are $a_M>0$, functions $u_N\in C_c^\infty(\operatorname{int}K;\mathbb C)$ for all integers $N\ge1$, and constants $C_m>0$ for all integers $m\ge1$, such that all $u_N$ have one fixed compact support and $\|u_N\|_{H^1}\le M$, $\|u_N\|_2=a_MN^{-1}$, and $\|R_\Theta u_N\|_D\le C_mN^{-m-1}$. Consequently, for every fixed $M>0$, no $\alpha>0$ and $C\ge0$ satisfy $\|u\|_2\le C\|R_\Theta u\|_D^\alpha$ for every smooth $u$ supported in $K$ with $\|u\|_{H^1}\le M$.
lem-ip-fourier-slice-identity-on-schwart:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$, $\theta\in S^1$, and $\sigma\in\mathbb R$, the one-dimensional Fourier transform in the offset variable, using the phase $e^{-2\pi i s\sigma}$, satisfies $\widehat{R_{\mathcal S}f}(\theta,\sigma)=\widehat f(\sigma\theta)$, where the two-dimensional transform uses the phase $e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}$. On compactly supported smooth inputs the formula has the same line parameterization and normalization as the Euclidean Radon transform.
prop-ip-limited-angle-fourier-visibility:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\Theta\subset S^1$ be a nonempty proper open antipodally symmetric set whose complement contains a nonempty open arc, and let $W_\Theta=\{\sigma\theta:\theta\in\Theta,\ \sigma\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\}$. For $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^2)$ and every measured normal $\theta\in\Theta$, the one-dimensional Fourier transform in the offset variable obeys $\widehat{R_{\mathcal S}f}(\theta,\sigma)=\widehat f(\sigma\theta)$ for all $\sigma\in\mathbb R$. In particular, zero restricted data imply that $\widehat f$ vanishes on $W_\Theta$. If in addition $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$, zero restricted data imply $f=0$ everywhere; this compact-support implication is proved separately from the choice-free compact-support Fourier-slice theorem and uses no Countable Choice.
